chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub from Muhammad ibn Yahya from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Muhammad ibn Sinan from Ibn Muskhan from Abd al-Malik ibn 'Amr: that he asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about Tamattu', so he said:

He said: 'Perform Tamattu'.' He said: 'It was concluded that he performed Hajj al-Ifrad in that year or after it.' I said: 'May Allah rectify you, I asked you and you ordered me to perform Tamattu', and I see that you have performed Hajj al-Ifrad this year.' He said: 'By Allah, the merit is in what I ordered you to do, but I am weak, so two circuits between As-Safa and Al-Marwah were difficult for me, therefore I performed Hajj al-Ifrad this year.'

key_terms.أَفْرَدَ: Performed Ifrad (a type of Hajj where one enters Ihram for Hajj only, without Umrah)
key_terms.اَلتَّمَتُّعِ: Tamattu' (a type of Hajj where one performs Umrah and Hajj separately with a break in between)
key_terms.بَيْنَ اَلصَّفَا وَ اَلْمَرْوَةِ: Between As-Safa and Al-Marwah (the ritual walking/running between these two hills)
key_terms.طَوَافَانِ: Two circuits (referring to the seven circuits of Tawaf performed during Umrah and seven during Hajj)

ai.seo_question: What is the difference between Hajj al-Tamattu' and Hajj al-Ifrad according to Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him)?
ai.summary: This narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* highlights the distinction between the general merit of Hajj al-Tamattu' and the specific flexibility of the Imam’s personal practice based on physical capacity. It illustrates the Shia scholarly principle that while Tamattu' is often preferred for its completeness, the Imam’s choice of Ifrad due to weakness serves as a valid precedent, demonstrating that religious rulings can accommodate individual circumstances without diminishing the virtue of the recommended act.
